artworks.title: Head Study of a Preacher
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink and gray wash on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Lowell Libson & Jonny Yarker, Ltd., in honor of Professor Donald Stone
artworks.description: The image shows an upper-body portrait of a man seated and leaning slightly forward, resting his arms on a surface in front of him. His facial features are distinct with a somewhat round face, broad nose, and pronounced brow. The man's expression appears focused, with his eyes directed forward. His hair is somewhat tousled and extends to his neck, peeking out from under a cap. He wears a traditional jacket and collar typical of historical attire, with visible folds and texture suggesting thickness and warmth. His hands are clasped, with an open book resting between them. The background of the image is subdued, with vague outlines suggesting the presence of other figures or people in silhouette, but with minimal detail.

artworks.title: Portrait of a Gentleman
artworks.medium: graphite on parchment (plumbago)
artworks.description: The image is an oval portrait showing the upper body of a person from the waist up. The individual is positioned facing slightly to the right but looks directly at the viewer. They have a full, round face with smooth skin and a neutral expression. The individual has long, curly hair that falls to the shoulders. They are wearing a dark, flowing garment with visible folds and a white neckcloth covering the neck. There is no visible jewelry or objects being held. The background is plain, making the subject the focal point of the image. The portrait is done in a monochromatic style.

artworks.title: Carte photographique de la lune, planche II (Photographic Chart of the Moon, plate II)
artworks.medium: photogravure with ink on tissue paper overlay
artworks.description: This is a photograph of the surface of the Moon. The image displays a detailed capture of the lunar surface, showcasing a landscape dominated by craters of varying sizes, some overlapping while others stand isolated. The texture of the lunar surface is rugged and uneven, revealing variations in shading that indicate the depth and contours of the terrain. The monochrome palette emphasizes the contrast between the cratered regions and the smoother plains. The arrangement and density of the craters suggest a heavily impacted surface over millions of years. The photograph includes text annotations detailing specific coordinates and technical information.

The photograph offers a striking view into the Moon's geology, capturing its pockmarked and barren appearance.
